Size of Supply Authority
Another difference in the supply authorities lies in their size. One Utility supplies over 1,500,000 consumers in an area the size, say, of Cornwall. At the headquarters they have a staff of clerks and receptionists, salesmen, engineers and teachers.

brief_extract:
B. JACKSON, first Chairman of the Trust Committee

" Electrical Times "

Choice Often Restricted
American Authorities frequently supply both gas and electricity, "pushing" gas for certain things and electricity for others, and it is by no means left to the choice of the individual consumer; although they believe gas will be completely out of date in less than ten years. Many companies do, however, allow a choice, many more sell exclusively electricity, and there is an enormous demand for electrical equipment.

SWEDISH HOMES FOR OLD PEOPLE

[Photograph: Swedish living room, with light coloured walls, divan, gay colours, and indoor plant.]

Swedish living room, with light coloured walls, divan, gay colours, and indoor plant. ONE of the most interesting aspects of Swedish life is the care for old people.

brief_context: A Swedish town mentioned for its attractive pensioner flats.
brief_extract:
In almost every Swedish town there are small estates of three-storied blocks of flats especially built for old age pensioners and let to them at very low rent. In Halmstad

Those in Halmstad are most attractive. The flats are well designed, and a really charming feature is the sitting room alcove at each end of every corridor.

brief_context: The author visited three housing estates for the elderly here.
brief_extract:
THE ELECTRICAL AGE. JANUARY, 1948

In Stockholm
In Stockholm I have visited three such estates. There are minor differences, such as a large concert hall with a stage and piano instead of separate sitting room alcoves.

brief_context: Mentioned regarding the role of house property managers.
brief_extract:
Women are employed to look after the estate, collect rent and keep an eye on the repairs, but they also take an interest in their tenants and often help them in many ways. Their work resembles that of house property managers in Britain. Special Hostel for the Old
In the hostel for the old they are looked after when they can no longer care for themselves.

brief_context: The author visited a new hostel for the elderly here.
brief_extract:
Special Hostel for the Old
In the hostel for the old they are looked after when they can no longer care for themselves. I visited a new one in Jönköping and was most impressed by everything I saw. The building itself is really attractive and is situated in a beautiful garden which, when properly cultivated, will make the hostel self-supporting in regard to fruit and vegetables.

brief_context: The author compares elderly homes with those in Sweden.
brief_extract: It is indeed a well and humanely run institution where the staff are devoted to making life as pleasant and easy as possible for the aged. When I think about many of the homes of the old people here and compare those in Sweden I look forward to a great extension of the many good schemes already in existence in England. 801

VESTING DAY

WHAT does Vesting Day mean
to the ordinary consumer of
electricity ? It means that on that
day, April 1st, electricity supply
in this country becomes the pro-
perty of the nation controlled by
a Central Authority and fourteen
area Electricity Boards. Up to
this date it has been in the hands
of municipal undertakings or com-
panies numbering about 550 in
all ; these will now no longer exist.

ship pays attention to the wel-

to research, especially in district
heating. The householders of Britain, in
thanking the Electrical Industry
for what it has done up till now,
greet the new Authority and wish
it well in this new venture, which
incorporates all that is best in the
past and makes provision for all
the best that is to come. 829

brief_extract:
A town of 50,000 people can
support a fine shopping centre. The existing centre of Crawley
will be incorporated in the new
plan, which provides those shops
and commercial buildings of
considerable architectural effect,
giving an atmosphere of civic
dignity. Education

The plan has provisionally
provided for three substantial
educational centres, which will in-
clude secondary education in all
its branches, community centres,

brief_context: Noted for its system of footpaths.
brief_extract:
Open Spaces
The plan will show a large number of open spaces, some of them collected in the form of parks accessible to the centre of the town, and others in the form of greens where local people with a short time to spare can find enjoyment and sunshine. Main roads will be bordered by trees and open spaces, and, it is hoped, a system of footpaths, for which Sussex is famous, will be continued in such a way that walks through green country and among trees can be a source of pleasure for the inhabitants over the whole area. There will be adequate provision for playing fields, allotments, and for local events.

location_standardised: London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Mentioned as part of a traffic route and motorway.
brief_extract:
Roads and Railways
Roads will be on the ring and radial principle, crossing the town without congesting the shopping centre. Through London-Brighton traffic will use the Crawley by-pass for the next few years, but a new London - Brighton motorway is planned to run east of the designated area, and when this is constructed (possibly in about 15 years’ time), this traffic will be diverted from the town entirely. The area is already very well served by railways, and as the town develops an even better service can be provided without difficulty.

brief_extract: The Company is one of the oldest and largest electrical concerns in the world. From its five great factories at Preston, Liverpool, Bradford, Rugby and Stafford, come every sort of electrical product, from a complete power station or a railway electrification scheme involving millions of pounds, down to the smallest fuse for domestic use. The Preston works were expanded enormously to produce large numbers of "Wellington" and "Halifax" bombers; now the vast spaces occupied by these have been swung over to the manufacture of electric trains, and of a range of domestic appliances, including cookers, fires, washing machines, water heaters, and a unique design of plate warmer.

brief_context: In context of national history and population.
brief_extract:
The Place of Electricity in History

Engineering has been one of the most formative and enduring of influences in our national history, and has in large measure determined the physical framework of our community life. The Roadmaking Engineer made possible the enduring pattern of Agricultural Britain. The Shipbuilding Engineer opened up the New World and the Seven Seas to our commerce and moulded our international destiny.

brief_context: Mentioned as opened up by the Shipbuilding Engineer.
brief_extract: The Roadmaking Engineer made possible the enduring pattern of Agricultural Britain. The Shipbuilding Engineer opened up the New World and the Seven Seas to our commerce and moulded our international destiny. The Steam Engineer gave us the network of railways, and made us the workshop of the world, thereby transforming both the distribution and the way of life of Britain's population.

brief_context: Location where first public electricity supply cables were laid.
brief_extract: Coal fires were used in this country in Roman times, but it was not until the middle of the 19th century that the real upturn in coal production began. It was not so much the discovery of induction, nor the introduction of the alternator, nor even the laying of the first public electricity supply cables in the gutters of Godalming, which inaugurated the Electrical Age, but rather the Grid system, by which the early promise of transmission and application of power was trans- lated into the beginnings of general availability to the com- munity. Electricity was already well established as a servant of the community, a number of large and efficient public generating stations had been built, and some interconnected networks had been established, but the standardisa- tion of frequency and the build- ing of the Grid in the 1930s marked the turning point of electrical progress.

"The Electrical Age" was fortunate in the ballot for tickets to visit the Atomic Energy Research Establishment at Harwell, which is working on the problem of the application of nuclear power to industrial purposes. Crown Copyright Reserved.

brief_context: Site of the Atomic Energy programme and nuclear piles.
brief_extract:
The training of Engineering and Craft Apprentices is an important part of the workshop organisation, and the scheme also provides for technical training of the boys from local schools and colleges. “ Gleep ” and “ Bepo ”

The first requirement of the Atomic Energy programme at Harwell is to build “ piles.” The first pile, Gleep (Graphite Low Energy Experimental Pile), is a simple unit designed to develop about 100 kilowatts of heat. It is used for measurement of the properties of atomic nuclei, for testing the nuclear properties of material used in the construction of piles, and for the production of radio-active isotopes for biological, medical, scientific, and industrial research.

brief_context: The origin of scientists who designed the Gleep pile.

It was designed largely by a New Zealand group of scientists working at Harwell, and considerable assistance was obtained from Canada. The second pile, Bepo (British Experimental Pile), was designed to develop 6,000 kilowatts of heat, and is larger and more complex.
